chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani and Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Aban, from Sulaym ibn Qays, who said:

I witnessed the bequest of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام when he bequeathed to his son al-Hasan عليه السلام, and he made al-Husayn عليه السلام, and Muhammad, and all of his children, and the chiefs of his Shi'ah, and the people of his household witnesses over his bequest.

Then he handed over to him the Book and the weapon, and said to his son al-Hasan عليه السلام: 'O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed me to bequeath to you, and to hand over to you my books and my weapon, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed to me and handed over to me his books and his weapon; and he instructed me to command you that, when death comes to you, you should hand them over to your brother al-Husayn عليه السلام.'

Then he turned to his son al-Husayn عليه السلام and said: 'And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed you to hand them over to this son of yours'—then he took the hand of Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام. Then he said to Ali ibn al-Husayn: 'And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed you to hand them over to your son Muhammad ibn Ali, and convey to him greetings from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and from me.'

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam Ali عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: the weapon transmitted as part of the Imamate trust
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the Book or written corpus handed down as part of the trust
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the succession from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام to the later Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the formal transfer of the sacred trust, including the books and weapon, from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام to al-Hasan عليه السلام, and then onward through al-Husayn عليه السلام, Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام, and Muhammad ibn Ali. It signifies the continuous designation of authority within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and preserves a witnessed account of succession.
